transcript.text:
Use the **Client Credentials grant flow** — PATs implicitly have this grant type, so no additional OAuth client configuration is needed.

## cURL

```bash
curl -X POST \
  'https://[tenant].api.identitynow.com/oauth/token' \
  -d 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  -d 'client_id={clientId}' \
  -d 'client_secret={clientSecret}'
```

Replace `[tenant]` with your ISC tenant name, `{clientId}` with the PAT's Client ID, and `{clientSecret}` with the PAT's Client Secret.

## Using the returned token

The response will contain an `access_token` (JWT). Pass it as a Bearer token in subsequent API calls:

```bash
curl -X GET \
  'https://[tenant].api.identitynow.com/v3/accounts' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer {access_token}'
```

## Notes

- The `access_token` expires per the `expires_in` value in the response (seconds).
- PATs do **not** return a `refresh_token` — you must re-request using the client credentials each time.
- The token carries the permissions of the ISC user who generated the PAT.

```answer-summary
    path: /oauth/token
    api_version: oauth
auth_flow: OAuth2 client credentials (PAT)
required_scopes: []
key_parameters: [grant_type, client_id, client_secret]
```
